messages:
erin: Quick sync: we need a short, operational play for post-launch triage that avoids constant roadmap churn. I propose 3 decision lanes and an explicit "freeze" trigger when reactive work exceeds budget.

noah: 👍 3 lanes = urgent hotfix, sprint fixes, and monthly batch for non-urgent enhancements. What should the freeze threshold be?

sophie: Suggest reactive budget = 22% of engineering capacity for first 8 weeks. If >22% for two consecutive sprints -> trigger pause and replan.

manu: From eng: require a 1-line dev-est on intake before any hotfix is scheduled. Also require a rollback path in the ticket (ff toggle or DB migration revert).

sam: Telemetry rules I can add: sustained error-rate >0.6% for 10m -> P1; customer complaint with repro + data loss -> P0. I'll wire alerts and a weekly reactive report.

erin: New rubric draft (compact):
P0: data loss/security -> immediate oncall, patch within 24h, owner: oncall
P1: core flow broken, no workaround -> triage within 4h, aim patch within 72h, owner: squad oncall
P2: degraded with workaround -> schedule next sprint unless >1% traffic -> hotfix window, owner: squad lead
P3+: enhancements/ux/perf -> monthly batch, owner: product grooming

noah: Add customer-tier override: Tier-1 customers (contract SLA) bump priority and can request expedited hotfix if tagged by CS. CS must attach contract citation.

sophie: Batch rules: monthly minor release, feature flags required, canary at 5% for 12h, smoke tests green -> full rollout. Cut branch 2 business days prior for testing.

manu: Hotfix rules: if quick-est > 4 dev-days, treat as P2 unless customer override. Also mandate test and rollback notes in PR description. Example rollback line: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api -n prod`

cs-bot: CS intake reminder: include customer-tier tag and contact. Template: https://redwood.internal/cs/intake-minimal (auto-post)

deploy-bot: Postlaunch runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/postlaunch-compact (auto-post)

erin: Action items: 1) sophie -> add capacity freeze rule & write short doc. 2) manu -> quick-est template + rollback snippet. 3) sam -> dashboards + weekly reactive digest. 4) noah -> add customer-tier override flow for CS. I'll schedule a 15m sync Tue 09:00 to ratify.

sophie: Confirmed, will draft the freeze gating language.

manu: Confirmed, will add the quick-est template to issue templates.

sam: Confirmed, will post initial dashboards in this thread when ready.

noah: Confirmed. I'll draft the CS escalation wording and the contracted-SLA tag behavior.

erin: Anything else? We should avoid making this process heavy, keep it clipboard-friendly for CS and engineers.

sophie: Agreed. Short checklists > long docs. I'll keep it to a single A4 and link to runbooks for details.

erin: Great. See you Tue 09:00. Drop edge cases here before then.
